messages.text: There’s a new decision of the two reviewers (last comment on #90), address it please
I’ll read the reviewers’ latest decision on PR #90 and work through the requested changes.

The reviewers agreed to move the inner and outer endcap stations outside the endcap toroids and form wheels of trapezoidal chambers without overlaps. They also want a new OBJ, full/endcap coverage estimates, and 2D chamber-shape inventories before and after.

I’ll check the available space against the calorimeters, coils and frame before choosing the new station positions.

The inner wheel has a space conflict: the HCAL ends at |z| = 6.4412 m and the endcap toroid starts at 6.55 m. After the existing clearances, only 8.8 mm remains for a 500 mm chamber. Which should change to make room?
- Adjust the endcap toroid’s axial extent and recalculate its field
- Keep magnets fixed and reduce the inner wheel’s radial reach around the HCAL

The agreed change exposes a real space conflict for the inner wheel: the HCAL–toroid gap is 109 mm, while the chamber is 500 mm thick. The outer wheel can fit beyond the existing frame, but requires a longer field map and simulation volume. I’m preparing the chamber inventories while the inner-wheel design choice is pending.
I’m using the ACTS Spack skill to verify the rebuilt environment before running the plots and propagation checks. The baseline inventory contains 816 barrel chambers and 744 endcap chambers.

The preflight registry still flags the updated setup and dependency lock as needing re-verification. I’m checking the current runtime directly; the ACTS rebuild completed yesterday. No dependency changes are needed for the inventory work.

The blue inventory sheets are generated: 6 barrel shape families and 18 endcap shape families. The clearance study also confirms that sector gaps can accommodate the barrel-toroid legs, but cannot solve the inner wheel’s lack of axial space. I’ll retain that distinction in the design note.

I’ve documented a concrete option that preserves the small-bore wheel: move the endcap toroid’s front return outward by 0.50 m, leaving its rear return fixed, then recompute the joint field and magnetic sizing. Keeping the magnets fixed instead requires a large inner opening and loses forward three-station coverage. I’m saving the inventories and interface evidence to PR #90; the revised OBJ and coverage scan await that design choice.

The inventory check reproduces all 1,560 source footprints and confirms the chamber counts. The previous ACTS evidence also still passes its checks. The prepared note explains why the new coverage comparison must use a longer field domain and a common launch surface, so it does not accidentally skip the inward-moved wheel.

The inventories and interface study are now pushed to PR #90. All 61 project and journal tests pass, along with the inventory, interface and retained ACTS checks. The requested revised layout remains pending the inner-wheel choice; the PR note identifies the new OBJ and coverage scan as unfinished.

Updated [PR #90](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/90#issuecomment-6283825776) with blue chamber inventories and the clearance study. All 61 project/journal tests pass.

The inner wheel cannot fit: **109 mm available versus 500 mm required**, before clearances.

I recommend shortening the endcap toroids by **0.50 m at their inner ends**, then recalculating the joint field. Should that change, or should we retain the magnets and enlarge the wheel’s opening, losing forward coverage?

The revised OBJ and coverage scan await this choice.
